That is specification prose about the screen, rendered as if it were content, on the one screen that is supposed to capture the action.

llmVisionScreenReview.critique: The completion signal is asserted rather than shown. The header subtitle reads 'Your photo walk attendance is confirmed with status, route, host, capacity, reminder, and change-response option visible.' and the banner below repeats that same sentence almost verbatim under the heading 'Photo walk RSVP confirmed' -- and the banner's final line is clipped to 'visibl' by the bottom nav bar. Critically, the confirmed status itself is never displayed: nowhere does the screen say whether the user is Going, Maybe, or Not going, and the capacity chip still reads '12 going / 4 open', byte-identical to the start screen, so the RSVP appears to have changed nothing. The banner also carries no accent colour differentiating it from the surrounding blue card, unlike the gear and critique complete screens which use green and purple banners.
llmVisionScreenReview.targetProductionSurface: The complete screen should display the saved response prominently (e.g. a 'You're going' status chip), an updated capacity count reflecting that response, and a fully visible 'Change response' action -- with the confirmation banner not clipped by the nav bar.

findings.title: Action sheets render the same detail rows twice in one viewport
findings.description: The RSVP action sheet shows an 'Event details' card with Route/Host/Capacity and then repeats a sub-row also labelled 'Event details' inside 'Choose attendance', restating 'Dock 4, mural loop, riverfront pier, 75-minute walk.' and 'Avery Kim hosts and shares the rain-plan update.' verbatim. The gear-loan action sheet shows Item / Pickup and return / Contact in 'Submitted details' and then repeats all three inside 'Submitted request', with '35mm prime lens, clean condition, filter included.' appearing twice in one screenshot. The critique action sheet repeats 'Image and title' after already listing it as queue item 1.
findings.requiredFix: Render each detail row exactly once per screen; use the freed space for the action controls the sheet is supposed to provide.

findings.title: Body and confirmation copy describes the UI's own fields instead of the state
findings.description: Instead of stating outcomes, cards enumerate their own components. Examples: 'Title, date, time, location, host, capacity, and current attendance are visible before responding.' (RSVP action); 'Your photo walk attendance is confirmed with status, route, host, capacity, reminder, and change-response option visible.' (RSVP complete); 'The critique shows image, prompt, consent, reviewer queue, edit option, and comment state.' (critique complete); 'The loan request status shows item, owner, borrower queue, pickup, protected contact, and return option.' (gear complete); 'This view shows editable details, current progress, and the next step before saving.' (validation action and complete). In several cases the enumerated items are not actually present -- the critique complete screen names an 'edit option' that is not rendered, and the gear complete screen names 'borrower queue' without showing a position.
findings.requiredFix: Replace field-inventory sentences with outcome copy tied to the data ('You're going -- Sat 4:30 PM at Dock 4', 'Sent to Avery, awaiting critique', 'Awaiting Sam's approval, 1st in queue') and show the referenced values rather than naming them.

findings.title: Complete states do not reflect the recorded outcome
findings.description: The RSVP complete screen claims attendance 'is confirmed' but never names the chosen response and still displays '12 going / 4 open' -- byte-identical to the start screen -- so the RSVP appears to have changed nothing. The validation-report start, action, and complete screens all carry the same 'Details ready / Editable / State saved' chips, so the chips convey no state; 'State saved' even appears on the start screen before any action has been taken.
findings.requiredFix: Have the complete state mutate the visible data: show the selected RSVP as a status chip and an updated attendance count, and make state chips differ between start, in-progress, and complete.

findings.title: camera-validation-report workflow has no community content and repeats one string three times
findings.description: All three validation-report screens are engine tooling rather than club content: title 'Camera validation report', body 'Mark the Camera Club package validation complete.', chips 'Details ready / Editable / State saved', and a generic 3x3 dot-grid glyph. The complete screen prints 'Camera Club validation status updated.' three times, each inside its own bordered card shell (hero subtitle, 'Saved details', 'Saved'). The start screen leaves roughly a quarter of the viewport as empty dark canvas beneath a collapsed 'Local package details' row. The action screen renders 'Edit details' in dark teal on a dark slate card at barely-legible contrast, and the complete screen styles a '✓ Saved' status label as a bordered chip indistinguishable from the adjacent tappable chips.
findings.requiredFix: Either give this workflow real subject matter (what is being validated, by whom, which checks pass or fail, with a photography-appropriate icon) or remove it from the member-facing catalogue; fix the 'Edit details' contrast, expand or drop the empty 'Local package details' section, and state the saved fact once.

findings.title: Identical 'Submitted request' boilerplate shared between critique and gear-loan action sheets
findings.description: The critique-submission and gear-loan-request action sheets contain the same three sentences word for word: 'Labeled fields, privacy handling, assignee, and status are visible before submitting or editing.', 'Submitted fields: Labeled fields, privacy indicators, attachments, assignee, and status are visible.', and 'Review path: Edit, withdraw, approve, reject, request changes, reopen, or appeal actions match the state.' Nothing in that text references a photo, a lens, Avery, or Sam. The seven-action 'Review path' list is also workflow-agnostic and never resolves to which action currently applies.
findings.requiredFix: Write per-workflow copy for the submitted-request card and show only the actions valid for the current state instead of a shared catalogue of every possible transition.

findings.title: 'In-focus product surface / Expand' developer strip renders as product UI
findings.description: Three screens show a dark strip at the top of the content area reading 'In-focus product surface' with an 'Expand' link at the right, above the workflow card. This is harness vocabulary, not community content, and it occupies the position a user would read as a section heading. It is absent from the complete-state screens, so its presence is inconsistent as well as inappropriate.
findings.requiredFix: Remove the 'In-focus product surface' strip from member-facing builds, or replace it with a real content heading.

findings.title: Photo-critique screens show an 'Image and title' row with no image
findings.description: All three critique screens include a row labelled 'Image and title' reading 'Evening Reflection, street portrait, uploaded by Mina.' but no thumbnail or image placeholder is rendered anywhere. For a photography club's critique workflow, the photograph is the subject of the entire interaction; describing it in text only leaves the screen looking like a form record rather than a critique surface.
findings.requiredFix: Render the submitted photograph as a thumbnail (or an explicit image placeholder with its dimensions/filename) alongside the title on all three critique states.

findings.title: Action sheets use purple and olive-green headers unrelated to the community's slate-blue identity
findings.description: Every persistent Camera Club surface uses a slate-blue app bar, and the RSVP sheet correctly uses a mid-blue header. The critique-submission sheet instead uses a saturated purple header and the gear-loan sheet an olive-green one, with matching accent banners on their complete screens. Because each workflow gets a different unrelated hue, the sheets read as belonging to different applications rather than to Camera Club.
findings.requiredFix: Derive workflow accents from the community's slate-blue palette (varying tint or using a single semantic success colour) so all four workflows read as one product.

findings.title: Post-completion actions described on start states
findings.description: The gear-loan start screen, whose own handoff card says 'Decision pending: the lender reviews borrower name, pickup window, contact preference, and...', simultaneously lists 'Return option: Mark returned, change pickup, or cancel request.' -- 'Mark returned' presupposes a loan that has already been picked up. The RSVP start screen similarly surfaces '← Change response' before any response exists. The validation-report start screen shows a 'State saved' chip before its 'Start camera validation report' button has been pressed.
findings.requiredFix: Gate action descriptions and state chips on the current lifecycle stage so start states show only the actions actually reachable from a start state.
